module rtlpp_00999 (
  Clk,
  Reset,

input wire Clk;
input wire Reset;
input wire CPU_Clk;
input wire CPU_M2;
input wire CPU_Rst;
input wire [14 : 0] CPU_Addr;
input wire [7 : 0] CPU_Data;
input wire CPU_RomSel;
input wire CPU_RW;
output wire [18 : 0] APU_Pulse1_Message;
output wire [18 : 0] APU_Pulse2_Message;
output wire [14 : 0] APU_Triangle_Message;
output wire [13 : 0] APU_Noise_Message;
output wire [3 : 0] APU_DMC_Message;

// Embedded 'nes_apu' module logic here
// Sample implementation of some logic, assuming some kind of audio processing
// The actual logic will depend on the detailed functionality of the 'nes_apu' module
reg [18:0] pulse1_message;
reg [18:0] pulse2_message;
reg [14:0] triangle_message;
reg [13:0] noise_message;
reg [3:0] dmc_message;

always @(posedge Clk or negedge Reset) begin
  if (!Reset) begin
    pulse1_message <= 19'b0;
    pulse2_message <= 19'b0;
    triangle_message <= 15'b0;
    noise_message <= 14'b0;
    dmc_message <= 4'b0;
  end else begin
    // Example placeholder logic, specific algorithm and operations should be defined according to the NES APU specifications.
    // The following logic is illustrative only.
    if (CPU_RW) begin
      pulse1_message <= {CPU_Addr[14: 0], CPU_Data[7: 3]};
      pulse2_message <= {CPU_Addr[13: 0], CPU_Data[6: 0]};
      triangle_message <= {CPU_Addr[14: 1]};
      noise_message <= {CPU_Addr[13: 1]};
      dmc_message <= CPU_Data[6:3];
    end
  end
end

assign APU_Pulse1_Message = pulse1_message;
assign APU_Pulse2_Message = pulse2_message;
assign APU_Triangle_Message = triangle_message;
assign APU_Noise_Message = noise_message;
assign APU_DMC_Message = dmc_message;

endmodule
